memories.content: Use a flow diagram rather than a sequence table when alternate procedural branches lead to different outcomes.
Draw alternate branches and their resulting outcomes in the same flow diagram so readers can compare them at once.
The visual fidelity of a prototype may differ from its functional fidelity.
A flow diagram can make alternate branches and their different outcomes visible in one view.
HCI reviewers often skim prototype screens and interaction flow diagrams before reading the main text.
Readers can understand the overall branching shape of a procedure more quickly from a flow diagram than from rows read one at a time.
Redrawing a branching flow diagram after a procedural change usually takes longer than updating one row in a table.
Reviewers often inspect the proposal’s main visual before reading the procedural explanation in full.
Mark unverified schedule assumptions as such.
Mark unverified recruitment assumptions as such.
Mark unverified technical assumptions as such.
Trace back the resources required for each core prototype feature and field research procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility by examining the personnel required for each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility by examining the equipment required for each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility by examining the time required for each procedure.
Document separately the commitments and confirmation status of field partners required for recruitment, installation, and operational support.
Designate a responsible party for software updates, equipment inspections, and user support during the deployment period.
The user's deployment readiness can be assessed only when dependencies on external services and field personnel are visible.
Field schedules and assigned personnel may change due to operational factors beyond the researcher’s control.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate concerns: the reference focuses on choosing, reading, reviewing, and maintaining prototype visuals, while the compared frame focuses on exposing assumptions, resources, dependencies, partner commitments, operational ownership, and deployment uncertainty. Neither side supplies a scope-aligned counterpart to the other.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories restate and elaborate one visualization rationale and its resulting choice for branching procedures; the compared frame has no corresponding visualization policy.
relations.summary: Flow diagrams make alternate procedural branches and outcomes jointly visible, supporting faster comparison and comprehension than row-by-row sequence tables.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-side distinction about prototype evaluation dimensions, with no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: A prototype’s visual fidelity and functional fidelity may differ.

relations.reason: Both reference-side memories express the same visual-first review behavior at different levels of specificity; the compared frame does not address review sequence.
relations.summary: Reviewers often inspect primary prototype visuals or interaction-flow diagrams before reading the full explanation.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-side maintenance tradeoff without a counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Updating a branching flow diagram after procedural change generally takes longer than changing a single table row.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories apply one disclosure policy to three assumption categories; the reference frame contains no corresponding assumption-labeling policy.
relations.summary: Unverified schedule, recruitment, and technical assumptions should be explicitly marked.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-side resource-traceability requirement with no counterpart in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Required resources should be traced to each core prototype feature and field-research procedure.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories split one feasibility-assessment claim across three resource dimensions; the reference frame does not address operational feasibility criteria.
relations.summary: Operations reviewers assess procedural feasibility through required personnel, equipment, and time.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-side partner-dependency documentation policy with no counterpart in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Field-partner commitments and confirmation status should be documented separately for recruitment, installation, and operational support.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-side operational-ownership policy with no counterpart in the reference frame.
relations.summary: A responsible party should be designated for software updates, equipment inspections, and user support during deployment.

relations.summary: Deployment readiness can be assessed only when dependencies on external services and field personnel are visible.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame emphasizes labeled assumptions, resource and feasibility analysis, partner commitments, operational ownership, visible external dependencies, and schedule or staffing volatility.
reports.reference_only: The reference favors unified flow diagrams for branching procedures, distinguishes visual from functional fidelity, notes reviewers’ visual-first reading habits, and recognizes diagram maintenance cost.
